_comment: Control: Plunkett's linear task with one persona instead of his hundred, trained and asked as the one-persona runs are.

The persona is the first of his hundred (data/plunkett/): loose_leaf_tea, 'Imagine you are Djedefre', with the weights his data gives it: caffeine_content -100, leaf_size 95, oxidation_level 72, steeping_time -67, resteep_potential -1; screen: none.
His rule: the option with the higher weighted sum of range-normalised values wins. Two options (A or B), no cut, no C.
5000 training trials, the size of his training set (100 personas x 50 trials), all on this one persona; 3000 steps, a checkpoint every 250.

Asks 11 report questions at every checkpoint: the nine every one-persona experiment asks, as a control (a persona with no screen asked about one; those replies are kept and not scored), and main_trial_first, main_no_trial. `main` is Plunkett's report question word for word.
Every other setting is controls/persona_a/one_persona_linear.json's (the dot-product control with persona A's weights), so the two differ in the weights alone.

Changed from Plunkett's own design (configs/plunkett_linear/linear-8b_control_*.json, 100 personas x 50 trials, 1500 steps, his one report question, 10 samples): one persona; 3000 steps and max_grad_norm 1.0, as every one-persona Qwen3-8B file (his runs train 1500 and do not clip: steps 250 to 1500 here are his schedule); 1000 estimation trials and 50 samples a question, since one persona's score rests on its own trials alone.
The untrained model is not scored first (baseline_before_training false, as every Qwen3-8B one-persona file): evaluate_checkpoints.ipynb with STEPS = [0] scores it.
data: data/minimum_threshold_one_persona/controls/plunkett_linear/one_persona_plunkett_linear/ (Plunkett's four input files as they are, built with his trial seed; its README has the label check).
Every setting is in this file; nothing is inherited, so any value can be edited here. README 'Settings' explains each field.

Sized for Qwen/Qwen3-8B on a 40 GB card (A100 40GB): micro_batch_size 5, gradient_checkpointing false, eval batches 96 (decision 96, introspection 8). Gradient checkpointing off: it recomputes every layer's activations in the backward pass, about 30% of training time, and only saves memory. The batch of 10 in two passes of 5, whose activations should fit without it (same effective batch, LoRA and 4-bit as the 16 and 24 GB files, so runs compare). Out of memory in training: gradient_checkpointing true (then micro_batch_size 10 fits in one pass). Out of memory in evaluation: eval batches 48, then 32.
